$description: Meta-schema for providers_fields.json — describes the metadata properties attached to every operations config field and how to interpret them.
$how_to_read: Each field in providers_fields.json carries metadata properties beyond 'type' and 'description'.
This file documents what those properties mean, what values they can take, and how to use them.
Start with 'visibility' → WHO is this field for?
Then 'mutability' → CAN I safely change this?
Then 'serialized' → WILL the database and config disagree?
Then 'affects' → WHAT system layers are impacted?
Then 'operation_type' → DOES this field drive an action or just describe/display?
Then 'triggered_by' → WHO or WHAT activates the behaviour this field controls?
Then 'overridable_per' → WHERE does the override live?
Then 'stability' → HOW SETTLED is this field?

visibility.purpose: Identifies the intended audience for this field's value or effect. Answers: 'Who is this for?'

user.meaning: The writer (end user) sees this field's value or its effect directly in the UI.
user.implication: Treat as user-facing copy or data. Changes affect what the writer reads.

developer.meaning: A developer or admin tunes this field to control engine behaviour. Not shown to end users.
developer.implication: Safe to change without copy review. Test the downstream effect.

system.meaning: Purely engine-internal. Consumed only by code.
examples: (most operations fields are developer-visible, few are pure system)
system.implication: Changes are invisible to users but can break internal contracts.

mutability.purpose: How and when this field can be changed. Answers: 'Can I safely change this, and what does it take?'

config.meaning: Change by editing the yml file. Takes effect on next server restart or config reload.

runtime.meaning: Can be changed via API or UI without restarting the server.

immutable.meaning: Changing breaks references in the database or other config sections.

affects.purpose: Which system layers are impacted when this field changes. Answers: 'What will be different?'

ai_pipeline.meaning: Changes LLM call behavior — model selection, prompt construction, tool availability.
ai_pipeline.how_to_verify: Re-run an AI task and compare outputs.

ui_display.meaning: Changes what the writer sees in the frontend.
ui_display.how_to_verify: Check the affected UI area in the browser.

data_model.meaning: Changes how data is structured, typed, or filtered.
data_model.how_to_verify: Check that existing DB records still load correctly.

performance.meaning: Changes speed, cost, or resource usage. No functional change.
performance.how_to_verify: Time operations before/after. Check API usage.

operation_type.purpose: Whether this field drives a mutation/side-effect or is read-only/informational. Answers: 'Does this DO something or just DESCRIBE something?'

action.meaning: This field controls behaviour that causes a side effect — an LLM call, a tool invocation, a data write, a retrieval query, an embedding computation.
examples: rag.rerank.enabled (triggers or skips an LLM reranking call)
tools.*.enabled (makes a tool available for invocation)
action.implication: Changing this field changes what the system DOES. Test by running the affected operation and observing side effects.

read.meaning: This field is informational — it configures a display, sets a label, provides a cost estimate, or documents intent. No side effects.
examples: rag.hybrid_alpha (weights a score calculation, no external call)
read.implication: Changing this field changes what the system SHOWS or how it SCORES, but doesn't trigger new operations.

gate.meaning: This field acts as a boolean or threshold gate — it doesn't perform the action itself but controls whether an action happens.
examples: providers.enabled (gates all calls to that provider)
gate.implication: Flipping a gate enables or disables an entire subsystem. Check what depends on the gated subsystem before toggling.

limit.meaning: This field caps or constrains an action — it doesn't trigger the action but bounds its scope, cost, or duration.
limit.implication: Changing a limit widens or narrows an existing operation. Too tight → truncation or timeouts. Too loose → cost or latency spikes.

operation_type.how_to_read: Ask: 'If I change this field, does the system call something new, stop calling something, or just change a number on screen?' action = new/different call. gate = enables/disables a call. limit = constrains an existing call. read = display/score only.

triggered_by.purpose: Who or what activates the behaviour this field controls. Answers: 'What sets this in motion?'

user.meaning: The writer triggers the operation — by clicking 'Run scan', 'Generate outline', asking a question in chat, etc.
examples: roles.model (used when writer triggers a scan or generation)
tools.search_tool (invoked when writer asks a question that needs retrieval)

ai.meaning: The AI engine triggers the operation autonomously — during a multi-step pipeline, an agent deciding to call a tool, or a background extraction pass.
examples: tools.style_meter (agent decides to check style during generation)
rag.rerank (engine runs reranking as part of retrieval pipeline)
tools.constraints_tool (agent decides to validate against rules)

cron.meaning: A scheduled background job triggers the operation — periodic re-indexing, embedding refresh, health checks.

startup.meaning: Triggered once at server startup or config reload — provider initialization, API key validation.
examples: providers.enabled (checked at startup to initialize provider connections)
providers.api_key_env (resolved at startup to load the API key)

triggered_by.how_to_read: Multiple triggers are common — a field like 'roles.model' is activated by user (manual scan), ai (agent tool call), and potentially cron (scheduled re-analysis). Read the list to understand all the entry points that exercise this field.

serialized.purpose: Whether this field's value is persisted to the database.

true.meaning: Stored in the database. Changing the config creates drift with existing DB records.

false.meaning: Lives only in the config file. Config is the single source of truth.
false.implication: Safe to change. New value takes effect on reload.

overridable_per.purpose: Whether per-project or per-lens overrides can replace the global value.

no.meaning: Global — all projects and lenses use the same value.

per_lens.meaning: A saved lens can override via chart_overrides.

experimental.meaning: May change shape or be removed.

notes.purpose: Free-form human context — trade-offs, edge cases, gotchas.

steps.question: DOES this DO something or just DESCRIBE?
WHO or WHAT sets this in motion?

patterns.meaning: A provider-level kill switch resolved at boot time. Flipping it requires a restart and affects everything downstream.
An LLM call or tool invocation that can be triggered both by the writer clicking something AND by the agent deciding autonomously.
A cap that trades completeness for speed/cost. Loosening increases quality but also cost and latency.
Background scheduled operations. Changes here affect automated jobs — check the cron schedule to understand timing.
Purely cosmetic user-facing data. Safe to change freely, only affects what the writer sees.
